l1_words.meaning: to attend or to watch (not to help)
to intend or aim to do something

pattern_explanation: These Portuguese words look almost identical to their English counterparts, but their core meanings differ, so the similar spelling makes them classic false friends rather than true cognates.
false_friend_warning: Students may think the Portuguese verb that resembles 'assist' means to help, but it actually means to attend or to watch. A learner might wrongly write 'I assisted the meeting' meaning they helped with it, when they only attended. The English word 'assist' means to help.
